response.text: Accrual and cash-basis accounting answer a simple question: when do you record money? With cash-basis, you record income when you actually receive cash and record expenses when you actually pay cash. It’s straightforward and shows what money is in the bank right now. With accrual accounting, you record income when you’ve earned it (for example, when you deliver a product or service) and record expenses when you incur them (when you promise to pay), even if the cash comes later. Accrual gives a clearer picture of how the business is doing over time because it matches the money you earned with the costs that created it. Cash-basis can make results jumpy if payments are delayed. In short: cash-basis shows cash flow; accrual shows economic activity. Use cash for simple, short-term tracking; use accrual to understand true performance and obligations.
